items.title: Joe Williams interviewed by Leslie Gourse, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: And the frozen frame at the end was a picture of Ellington, Woody Herman and I with our arms around each other, and we are laughing you know.

ctx.x: No, no, no, no. Ellington wrote a thing called “Koko,” which somebody later stole and used it. They always used things of his though. Like “Night Train” is the fourth tenor part of “Happy Go Lucky” of Ellington’s. But who was it that did [scats] Great line. Then Joe Nanton came in [scats].
Oh you’re marvelous. You’re a whole band.
